title: Exact S4 cost: two double-transposition targets need eight calls
body:
## Result

In the explicit formal `F2[S4]` model with three dirty scalar roles, free `GL3(F2)` mixing, and unit-cost paid adjacent transpositions `(12),(23),(34)`, the target `diag([(13)(24)],[(13)(24)],[e])` has exact minimum 8 calls. Its direct cost is 8, while the natural-representation displacement-rank floor is only 4, leaving a concrete two-call sharing gap to test.

The sign determinant over `F2[C2]` forces every valid word to have even length, so a strict improvement would require at most 6 calls. A complete exact radius-three meet over all 84 involutive factors contains 237,474 formal states on each side and has empty intersection. Thus no word of length at most 6 exists. The direct 8-call group-algebra identity supplies the matching upper bound.

This changes the target cycle type from the two 4-cycles in [PR #1720](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1720), where displacement rank matches direct length. Here each double transposition has Coxeter length 4 but displacement rank 2. The result closes only this fixed target/alphabet/role model.

## Reproduction and provenance

```sh
python3.12 -I -B research/s4-double-transposition-seedb270/verify.py
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/s4-double-transposition-seedb270 --check-only
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/s4-double-transposition-seedb270
```

The registered replay passes. Exact ball counts, deterministic state hashes, eight call-omission controls and the altered dirty-role control are recorded in the package. The package pins base `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`, accepted bit-mechanisms seed `b270b3b52d302ab6281ea2bc042d4aea`, priority revision 3 and selected-record SHA-256 `10b9e340fd8e354a37a0c4813c90e5de1dd42044b5f6aca4a3fc5a42b685fa32`.

The selected binding-only baseline remains complex-primitive-bound. This abstract finite address model is not mapped to a supplier and makes no recursive-moment or κ claim. No selected source, certificate or frontier is changed. The completed finding is recorded in [coordination Discussion #1163](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1163#discussioncomment-18919260). Prepared by Cinna Davis with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, disclosed in `TASK.json`; no subagents or independent human review.
